https://www.theguardian.com/news/audio/2.text: 00:00:00 00:00:00 Today in Focus West Bank The Palestinian school under siege – podcast At least five pupils at a village school in the West Bank have been killed in the last year by settlers and soldiers. Emma Graham-Harrison reports on how the school found itself on the frontline, while a teacher explains what life is like for staff and students. More ways to listen Apple podcasts Spotify RSS Feed Download Presented by Annie Kelly with Emma Graham-Harrison ; produced by Ivor Manley and Brian McNamara ; executive producer Homa Khaleeli Tue 15 Sep 2026 22.00 EDT Share Waheed Abu Naim is an English teacher at the Al Mughayyir boys’ school in a village in the West Bank . He loves his job, he says. “I am happy to be a teacher. Although we don’t get lots of money, because my students, especially in the morning, wait for me when I enter the school to shake hands, to smile at me while going inside their classes. So it’s a happy life.” But the last year has been anything but happy for Waheed. His village is now surrounded by settlers, while the military has blocked off every road except one, which has a checkpoint on it. Teachers who live in neighbouring villages cannot always come to work. But worse are the attacks on the village by settlers. In April, a 14-year-old pupil was killed next to a playground gate after a gunman opened fire. As Waheed rushed the teenager to hospital he learned his own brother had also been killed. Senior Middle East correspondent Emma Graham-Harrison tells Annie Kelly : “We’ve documented the hundreds of children who’ve been killed by Israeli soldiers, settlers over the last three years. But even in that context, of sort-of regular deadly violence, there is something particularly horrific about someone taking aim at a school full of children.” Four other students were also killed and, says Emma, things don’t seem to be getting better. “In the next few months I’m just, very unfortunately, expecting to see at least the same level of violence and frankly, probably an escalation.” Photograph: Alaa Badarneh/EPA Explore more on these topics West Bank Today in Focus Israel Middle East and north Africa Palestine Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9zr.text: Figure caption, Watch: BBC tracks down abusive teacher secretly released early By Endang Nurdin Â and Â Rebecca Henschkeâ¯ ,Â BBC Eye Investigations Published 21 September 2026, 00:12 BST An Indonesian teacher convicted of sexually assaulting a student at an Islamic boarding school has been secretly released from prison early, a BBC Eye investigation has found. Moch Subchi Azal Tsani or Bechi, as he is known, is the son of an influential Islamic religious leader. His trial sent shockwaves through Indonesia, a Muslim-majority country where millions of parents send their children to Islamic boarding schools. He was arrested in 2022 at his father's school in East Java where he had taught, after a 15-hour siege involving nearly 1,000 riot police - his family's supporters had gathered in large numbers to prevent his arrest. He was sentenced to seven years in prison later that year. The government withdrew the school's operating licence, but then President Joko Widodo intervened to keep the school open, arguing that the case involved an individual rather than the institution. But our investigation has uncovered further allegations against Bechi, 46, and evidence suggesting that the school and the family attempted to suppress them. Bechi's release comes as the National Commission on Violence against Women warns of an "emergency" of sexual violence in Islamic boarding schools. It says the power of religious leaders is shielding these schools from oversight and repercussions, while discouraging students from reporting abuse. Image caption, Bechi was recorded at an event earlier this year by BBC reporters who were undercover Of the several female students who alleged abuse and rape against Bechi, only one pursued a legal case that led to him being convicted. Her identity has never been made public. Prosecutors sought the maximum sentence â 16 years â for rape, but the court found Bechi not guilty of rape, and convicted him for the lesser charge of sexual assault. Undercover footage recorded by the BBC now reveals that he has been released after serving less than half his sentence. Catching My Teacherâ¯ Two ex-students expose sexual abuse by teachers at Islamic boarding schools in Indonesia Watch on iPlayer Listen on Sounds Viewers in the UK can also watch Catching My Teacher on Global Eye on BBC Two at 19:00 BST. Outside the UK, watch on YouTube , external . Bechi would have been eligible for parole around March 2027, or would have been released at the end of his sentence in 2029. Indonesia's Ministry of Immigration and Corrections told the BBC that Bechi was released in August 2025 because of "sentence remissions granted to him in accordance with applicable regulations". The ministry said it could not say why his sentence was reduced. Ira Puspitasari was another student who testified at the trial, but her allegations didn't lead to separate charges. She waived her legal right to anonymity to speak publicly about this for the first time. "I was treated as his slave. I was held captive, raped, beaten," she says. "I can never forget what he said to me: 'Don't you realise you're just my slave?'" After watching the undercover footage of Bechi smiling and greeting supporters at an event in March, she tears up and says: "It's like nothing ever happened." Ira told the BBC she was raped and sexually abused by him for more than four years, from the time she was 15 years old. She said she tried to run away but Bechi's private security guards tracked her down, kidnapped her and took her to a secluded hut, where Bechi tortured and raped her.â¯ She said she was then expelled from the school. She said she reported all of this to the police but was then intimidated into withdrawing her police report. She shared an audio recording of Bechi's mother telling her to say that "nothing had happened". Image caption, Ira is speaking publicly for the first time about her allegations against Bechi In January this year, after hearing that Bechi may have been released early, BBC undercover reporters attended an annual prayer event at the Shiddiqiyyah Islamic boarding school in East Java. The reporters saw Bechi wearing a mask and sitting beside his father. Just before he appeared on stage, filming and photography was prohibited, a marked difference from previous years. Then in March, BBC reporters again captured Bechi on hidden camera at another prayer event for Eid at his family home located in the same compound as the school. The BBC sought comment from Bechi, his mother and the Shiddiqiyyah school but there has been no response. The students who testified, including the girl he was convicted of sexually assaulting, were placed under witness protection and Indonesian law requires them to be informed of Bechi's release. But they were not informed, Ira and another former student who testified told the BBC. They were stunned by the undercover footage of Bechi because they believed he was still in prison. The ministry said that victims need not be informed because Bechi remains on parole, but the witness protection agency disputed this, saying the victims must still be informed. Ayu Masuroh says she was never abused by Bechi but she started investigating the allegations of abuse against him after hearing about them from schoolmates. She lives close to the school and says she is frightened about Bechi being out of prison. "He hates me. His supporters have threatened to kill me many times. I will never feel safe here. I don't feel safe living in Indonesia." Speaking publicly for the first time, she told the BBC she collected testimonies from at least 10 other female students, all of whom alleged that they were sexually assaulted or raped by Bechi. According to her, some said Bechi told them they were "chosen", and one of them said Bechi raped her after calling her for a "personal interview". These accounts were part of the closed-door trial, which alleged years of abuse at the school, according to court records seen by the BBC. Image caption, Ira and Ayu both testified at Bechi's trial - and say they didn't know he had been released early until they saw the BBC footage Nun Sayuti, a former lawyer for the school who later left and began supporting the students, says he is "deeply disappointed" by Bechi's early release, which is a "violation of victims' rights. They went through a long and difficult legal process to bring this case to light". He, too, testified at trial. He told the court that when the rape allegations first surfaced, Bechi ordered him to make them go away. But when he started investigating the claims, he says he realised he was defending the wrong side and "knew I had to take a stand". Nun then started collecting evidence and before leaving the school secretly recorded Bechi boasting.â¯In the recording the BBC has heard, he says: "In my position, I can have my way with anyone I want." The cases that have come to light across Indonesia in recent years may be just the "tip of the iceberg", the commission on violence against women, or Komnas Perempuan, warned in a statement in May. Students in many schools are unable to report abuse because of inadequate protection mechanisms, it said, and called on the government to strengthen oversight and impose stronger penalties so that religious leaders cannot exercise unchecked power. Bechi's case is one of Indonesia's most high-profile sexual abuse scandals, given the political influence his father wields. Kiai Muchtar Mu'thi combines Islamic teachings with a strong emphasis on Indonesian nationalism, and the school he owns in East Java is part of a wider complex that has thousands of loyal followers. Bechi had been teaching at the school for at least a decade when he was arrested in 2022 despite public opposition. Hundreds of students and supporters gathered behind the gates of the school to prevent police from entering. They stood shoulder to shoulder, raising their fists and chanting that they were prepared to defend the school "with body and soul". Image source, ANTARAFOTO/Didik Suhartono Image caption, Bechi was arrested in 2022 - and tried and convicted shortly after Over the years, Muchtar and his school â as well as the Shiddiqiyyah complex it sits in â have drawn public figures looking for support in what is a key political battleground. In 2014, then-presidential candidate Joko Widodo visited during his political campaign. Five years later, his successor Prabowo Subianto did the same. Indonesia's national police chief visited the school and met Muchtar in August last year, saying he wanted to forge closer ties with Shiddiqiyyah. It was the family's connections and clout that Ira says persuaded her to withdraw her allegations against Bechi. "I was terrified," she told the BBC, adding that it escalated as his supporters began giving her death threats. In June 2018, Ira and her father were summoned to a hotel near the school, she says, where she met Bechi's mother, Nyai Shofwatul Ummah. Ira secretly recorded their conversation and shared it with the BBC. In it Bechi's mother says that her son had "made mistakes, perhaps in his relationship with Ira. So I apologise". She then urges Ira to withdraw her police report. "Nothing happened, it's only family business," she tells her. Ira says that fearing for her safety, she signed a statement retracting her allegations, which she now regrets. When the case went to trial, Ira says she was questioned for hours, where they "asked these really probing questions â very painful questions. I told the court everythingâ. Now watching the footage of Bechi out of prison, she says, "it feels as if he has won and I've lost". "It's very important the world knows. It's true. He is free. It's just a complete mockery of the law." https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/11/19/alek.text: Aleksandar Čupićot választotta meg a szerb parlament többsége a házelnöki posztra csütörtökön. A nyilvános szavazás során 97 fő voksolt a volt kormánypárt jelöltjére, az Egyetemista Lista képviselőjének pedig 140 fő szavazott bizalmat. Ez egyben azt is jelenti a rendkívüli helyzet miatt, hogy Čupić egyben – ha csak átmeneti jelleggel is – elfoglalhatja az államfői széket. Ugyanis Aleksandar Vučić szeptember 27-én lemondott , hogy egy esetleges győztes választás után átüljön a kormányfői székbe, azóta – ahogy az a magyar alkotmányosságban is bevett gyakorlat – a parlament házelnöke tölti be ideiglenesen a posztot. Ez eddig Ana Brnabić volt, de az új parlament új házelnököt választott. Čupić a december 27-i választás utánig, a megválasztott új köztársasági elnök beiktatásáig tölti majd be a pozíciót. Čupić a belgrádi Közlekedéstudományi Egyetem docense, több mint húsz éve tanít az intézményben. Az első pillanattól kezdve támogatta az egyetemista mozgalmat: amikor 2025 februárjában több száz egyetemista gyalogolt a dél-szerbiai Kragujevacba szervezett tüntetésre, Sopoton, ahol a családjával él, megszervezte mindannyiuk szállását és ellátását. Az ország nyilvánossága a választási kampányban figyelt fel rá, amikor öblös hangján többször is a Vučić elleni tüntetések egyik himnuszává vált Szerbia ébred című dal közös éneklésére buzdította az egybegyűlteket. Az egyetemfoglalásokból és tüntetésekből kinőtt Egyetemista Lista (SL) 140, az Aleksandar Vučić volt köztársasági elnök nevével fémjelzett, a korábban kormányzó Szerb Haladó Pártot (SNS) is maga mögött tudó Egyesült Szerbia pedig 103 mandátumot szerzett . A 250 tagú szerbiai parlament fennmaradó hét mandátumán öt kisebbségi lista osztozik: a Vajdasági Magyar Szövetség (VMSZ) és az Albán Koalíció 2-2 mandátumot nyert, három bosnyák lista pedig 1-1 mandátumhoz jutott. Az Egyetemista Lista más pártok támogatása nélkül is képes lehet az új kormány megalakítására, amihez legalább 126 képviselő támogatása szükséges. A kormányalakítás kérdéseiről és az új kormány előtt álló legfontosabb feladatokról itt írtunk bővebben . Az új házelnök megválasztása a parlament maratoni alakuló ülésének legfontosabb aktusa volt. Ugyanakkor abszolút nem ment le gyorsan a folyamat, ugyanis az ellenzékbe szorult Szerb Haladó Párt (SNS) és szövetségesei láthatóan szándékos obstrukcióval lassították az alakuló ülést. Vučić hétfőn 1 óra 40 perces beszéddel fárasztotta hallgatóságát, a pártjához kötődő ideiglenes házelnök, Stojan Radenović többórás szüneteket rendelt el. Vučić a második, szerdai ülésnapon is harmincszor kért szót, ebből egyszer 40 percig beszélt. Annak ellenére, hogy sem a volt elnök, sem a volt kormánypárt többi felszólalója nem tartotta magát a napirendi ponthoz, és a legkülönfélébb témákat kezdték el boncolgatni, az ülést levezető Radenović egyiküket sem figyelmeztette, és nem vette el tőlük a szót. Végül a szerdai ülés végéhez közeledve az Egyetemista Lista (SL) egyik képviselője, Jugoslav Gašić bejelentette, hogy annak érdekében, hogy mielőbb megválasszák az új házelnököt, egyetlen képviselőjük sem kíván felszólalni az első napirendi pont ügyében. Az ülés végén aztán az SL képviselői tiltakozásul egyszerre a magasba emelték a házszabályt tartalmazó könyvecskét. Az Egyetemista Lista frakcióvezetője, Jovo Bakić szerdán bejelentette, hogy a parlament alelnökeinek a Szerbiában élő kisebbségek sorából való képviselőiket fogják javasolni, miután azok a körzeteikben „fölényes győzelmet arattak” a kisebbségi listák jelöltjei fölött. Az SL listáján bejutott magyarok közül még nem tudni, ki lesz az, mert zajlik a választás. Az új szerb kormánynak a parlament megalakulása után legkésőbb 90 nappal fel kell majd állnia.

Skip next section ANALYSIS: Steinmeier promotes Africa to German business community 11/24/2026 November 24, 2026 ANALYSIS: Steinmeier promotes Africa to German business community Rosalia Romaniec in Abidjan Steinmeier met his Ivorian counterpart Alassane Ouattara Image: Bernd von Jutrczenka/dpa/picture alliance The Federal President’s latest major trip takes him to Africa. Frank-Walter Steinmeier has just visited the Ivory Coast and is continuing on to Ghana and Kenya. His goal: to encourage more German companies to invest in Africa. Frank-Walter Steinmeier has visited 31 African countries during his political career. Even as foreign minister, he traveled regularly to the continent; as federal president, he has made twelve trips so far. From early on, he viewed Africa not only through the lens of development aid and humanitarian support, but also — much like former Chancellor Angela Merkel — as a market for the German economy that has been underutilized thus far. In 2015, as foreign minister in the Merkel administration, Steinmeier played a central role in the creation of the German-African Economic Summit. German businesses should take more risks On his current trip as well, Steinmeier is advocating for greater German engagement in Africa . In Abidjan, the capital of the Ivory Coast, following a meeting with Ivorian President Alassane Ouattara, he called on German companies to step outside their comfort zone and take greater advantage of the opportunities offered by the country and the continent. The Ivory Coast is considered a location with growing potential. Despite its proximity to the Sahel region, which is plagued by terrorism, the country is relatively stable politically. The economy is growing by about six percent annually. Germany has more intensive trade relations with the Ivory Coast than with any other country in sub-Saharan Africa, and nowhere else in sub-Saharan Africa do so many people learn German — an advantage for German small and medium-sized enterprises — all of which both presidents emphasized very clearly during their meeting in Abidjan. Steinmeier's final Africa tour as president will include the Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya Image: Bernd von Jutrczenka/dpa/picture alliance Up next, Steinmeier is scheduled to visit Accra, Ghana , for the sixth German-African Economic Summit, where more than 600 business representatives are expected to attend. As the summit’s initiator, the Federal President will open the event together with the host, Ghanaian President John Mahama. He will be accompanied by a ten-member business delegation representing industry, the financial sector, and energy consulting. Africa as an economic partner The Economic Summit is taking place at a time when Germany’s relations with African countries are undergoing fundamental changes. In light of geopolitical shifts, Africa is increasingly coming into focus as an economic and trade partner. The continent’s share of German foreign trade currently stands at just under 2%, or around €30 billion. At the same time, German exports to Africa are rising by at least 6% annually. And since Germany’s economy aims to reduce its dependence on China in the future, opportunities in Africa are growing . From Ghana, Frank-Walter Steinmeier will travel on to Kenya , the final stop on his tour of Africa. At the 2008 summit in Bucharest, Romania , German Chancellor Angela Merkel and French President Nicolas Sarkozy argued that they weren't ready to extend NATO membership to Ukraine. US President George W. Bush said he was in favor of having Ukraine enter into NATO. But both Germany and France said that that would hurt relations with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The NATO summit then decided that Ukraine would eventually join the alliance , but offered no timetable. At a press conference on Monday, Merz was asked about whether he thinks the time was right to talk about Ukraine's membership in NATO. To which Merz said, "If it [Ukraine] had become a member of NATO, this war could probably have been prevented." Merz meant Russia's war against Ukraine when he said "this war" at the press conference after a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. Angela Merkel defended her decision at the Bucharest summit as of 2024 as well, saying a large proportion of the Ukrainian population had opposed joining NATO at the time. Edited by: Jenipher Camino Gonzalez https://p.dw.com/p/5PmLK Skip next section German tech startup investments see sharp rise, study finds 11/23/2026 November 23, 2026 German tech startup investments see sharp rise, study finds Sertac Comak Boom being driven by companies specializing in AI, humanoid robotics and defense technology Image: Marco Einfeldt/SZ Photo/picture alliance German startup investments in fields such as robotics and defense are set to almost triple this year, a study noted on Monday. The German Start-up Association and the Joachim Herz Foundation study predicted that investments in so-called "deep tech startups" will surge from just €2.9 billion ($3.17 billion) last year to 8.1 billion ($8.9 billion) this year. The study described the rise as a "major success for Germany as a business location." "Deep tech" typically refers to developing cutting-edge technologies based on scientific research, such as AI, biotechnology and quantum computing. A handful of massive fundraising rounds by firms including humanoid robot developer Neura Robotics, AI drone maker Helsing and defense tech group Quantum Systems drove the investment boom. The study also showed about 300 new deep tech startups are expected to be founded this year, a 40% rise compared with last year. Newly found startups tend to be founded around economic hubs like Berlin and Hamburg, which are also home to leading universities and research institutes. The study also highlighted challenges, including limited funding compared with their US counterparts and insufficient support to move startups from the laboratory to the real world.
